sections.title: Shrub and leaves
sections.text: Trevoa quinquenervia, the Chilean tralhuén, is a perennial, deciduous, thorny shrub reported to reach about 3 m. Its small, elliptic leaves are 1–3 cm long, with five (sometimes seven) veins and a pale, hairy underside.

sections.title: Flowers and identification
sections.text: Short flowering shoots carry small clusters of pale flowers. The crossed spines and narrow, five-veined leaves in the plate match the species. It is native to Chile; no food use is established in the cited floras.
